_meta.title: Style Anchor — Majority Master Instructions & Per-Series Deviations
_meta.purpose: For each subject and phase/level, gives the MAJORITY value of each tracked field across ALL same-level modules in that subject (the 'master_instructions' a brand-new module SERIES must adopt), PLUS a per-existing-series record of where that series' most-recent module DEVIATES from the master (the 'series_deviations' a NEXT module in that existing series must match instead). Built on the same level-scope strategy as Style_Anchor_Registry_Level_Scope.json.
_meta.source: Per-module Stage-1 summaries in All_Template_Reports (amalgamated 11-field model: 6 scalar + 5 cross-page pattern fields).

the_two_rules.1_new_series_uses_majority: When an ENTIRELY NEW base series is created at a level (e.g. OSAX201 in a subject that has no OSAX yet), apply the master_instructions — the majority value of each field across every same-level module in the subject.
the_two_rules.2_existing_series_matches_sibling: When the NEXT module in an EXISTING series is created (e.g. OSAI202 after OSAI201), it MUST match that series' established pattern exactly. Where that pattern deviates from the master, the deviation is listed under series_deviations for that base; the next module follows the deviation, NOT the master. Sibling consistency overrides the majority — this is the most important rule.

how_to_apply.resolve_field: For a module of base SERIES + LEVEL: start from master_instructions for that subject+phase; then if the base series appears in series_deviations, overlay (override) those fields. The result is the full style ruleset that module must follow.
how_to_apply.new_series: A brand-new base series (one not listed in series_deviations) simply uses master_instructions as-is.
how_to_apply.existing_series: The next module in an existing series uses master_instructions overlaid with that series' deviating_fields, so it stays consistent with its established siblings.

_meta.field_model: Scalar fields hold one value; pattern fields (module_code, h1_count, menu_type, menu_button_tooltip, footer_links) hold an {overview, lesson[, final]} object compared as a whole.
_meta.stage1_note: CONVERTER_V2 Stage-1 optimised copy: tekuradev normalised to tekura; deviations that became identical to the master after normalisation were removed (they are no longer deviations). See STAGE1_DATA_CHANGELOG.md.
